steps.content: The night is silent, like a drop of wine sealed in glass.
Cassian stands before the door and knocks. Two soft "thud, thud" sounds fall, followed by faint stirring from within. A moment later, the door opens.
Falke slouches against the table, a silk robe hanging loose on his shoulders. He has the look of an old beast, smug and sated after feasting on a prey. He glances at Cassian, his tone dismissive.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: Room service? I didn't order anything.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: My apologies for the intrusion. This is a complimentary offering from Euphoria for our most distinguished guests.

With Falke's nod of approval, Cassian steps inside, his head bowed, and sets a silver tray down on the table. It holds a drink of his own concoction. He uncorks the bottle and pours a glass. The amber liquid swirls, its rich aroma almost overpowering the faint scent of rot in the air.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: It's your usual blend. I've taken the liberty of making some minor adjustments. I added... something better suited for memories.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: Oh?
He lifts the glass, takes a sip, and raises an eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: Not bad at all. When did you come aboard? I don't think I've seen you before.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I'm a recent hire.
Cassian's voice stays calm and steady in the dim, hazy lights of the VIP suite. He slowly raises his head, revealing the horrendous scars on his burned face.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: But I think you have seen me before. You've simply forgotten.
Falke freezes, his expression cracking.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: You are...

Before he can finish, Cassian runs a finger along the rim of the glass. A wisp of vapor rises, and the bouquet twists into invisible blades, piercing deep into Falke's mind. The man's face contorts. The glass slips from his fingers and shatters on the floor.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: What is this... you... you're—!
He finally recognizes the face, the eyes of the boy who once pleaded at his feet. A pained groan escapes Falke's lips as his consciousness splinters under the psychic assault.
Cassian watches coldly, the liquor dancing on his fingertips. All he can see are the shadows of his own past, stretching across an endless night.
On his first day aboard the ship, he'd played the piano and mixed drinks with every ounce of skill he had, all to secure a position on Euphoria.

steps.speaker: Recruiter
steps.content: That scar's an eyesore. Skills are mediocre at best. The only things you've got going for you are these hands... pale, slender fingers, well-proportioned.
He ran his fingers over Cassian's knuckles, examining them like merchandise at an auction. Suddenly, his tone shifted, and he clicked his tongue in mock pity.

steps.speaker: Recruiter
steps.content: Such a shame... They're not soft enough.
Without warning, the man's hand clenched. He snapped Cassian's little finger with a sickening crack.

Cassian let out an agonizing scream. He struggled, but the guards behind him held him fast. Thumb, index finger, middle finger, ring finger. Then the other hand. The excruciating pain seemed to have no end.
Finally, they dumped his limp body in the garbage-strewn rear cabin, like a broken doll.

steps.speaker: Recruiter
steps.content: Don't give me that look. I'm just putting you where you belong. Sleep tight, Mr. Cassian. May you be worth something in your next life.
And earlier, when his family was crushed by false accusations, Cassian had knelt before Falke's expensive leather shoes in his father's old formal suit.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: Begging me? What good will that do? Fate decided that you and your family would serve me. It also decided how you would make your exit.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: If you must hate something, hate yourselves. You weren't born as hawks. No matter how high you climb, you're still doomed to fall to your death.

steps.speaker: Falke
steps.content: Try not to be born in the gutter next time. Now, say your prayers. Serve me one last time.

Then came the screams, the wails, the roaring fire. Through the smoke and ash, his mother's scalding hands touched his burning, bleeding face. "Live," she whispered, before shoving him away, vanishing forever into the void of memory.
Cassian clenches his fist. The amber liquor rises into the air, writhing and contorting before plunging into Falke's eyes, his ears, his nostrils, his mouth.
Falke howls, toppling over his chair. He convulses madly on the floor, his throat producing only torn grunts as he plummets, struggles, drowns in illusions.
Cassian stands motionless, his eyes calm, as though he's looking at someone long dead. He steps forward, crouches, and leans close to Falke's ear.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Do you remember? You told me to pray and serve you one last time. So here I am. This judgment... this is the last service you'll have from me.

Several days later
Eastside Hospital
Cassian gets up. He pulls the IV needle from his arm and disconnects the monitors. He takes his clothes from the locker, changes, and quietly slips out of the room.

His last memories of Euphoria are vague. The last thing he remembers is steering the boat carrying the three of them away from the quicksand before exhaustion claimed him. How he got out of WhiteSands, how he ended up back in Eastside... he has no idea.
But none of that matters anymore.
Cassian walks the streets of Eastside like a ghost drifting among the living. Pedestrians hurry past, all of them strangers, indifferent to the story of someone whose shoulder they just brushed.
Only the massive electronic billboard overhead is still tirelessly cycling through the news...

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>[WhiteSands Cruise Ship Explodes, Dozens Missing]</color>

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>[Eastside Official Falke Survives Explosion, in Critical Care with Severe Mental Trauma]</color>
Cassian stares at that familiar face.
The hypocrite who once stood in the light and preached about "justice" now lies inert in a hospital bed, riddled with tubes. People speak of him with a mixture of shock and pity.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I won.
He mutters to himself, his words drowned in the city's din.
He remembers himself from years ago, staggering down these same streets, bruised and broken and barely clinging to life, his tattered coat doing little to shelter his skinny frame.

He'd stood beneath this very screen, watching that same man give a smiling interview about "stabilizing the situation" and rooting out "the corrupt parasites." In that moment, hatred had burned like a fire in his blood.
Cassian had imagined his vengeance countless times, fantasizing about dragging that man from his pedestal, watching him weep and beg for mercy.
But now that the fire has burned out, he feels nothing but emptiness.
It's like a piece of his heart is missing, leaving him too numb even for pain. He doesn't know where to go, or what to do next.
His feet carry him, unbidden, to the roof of a skyscraper. He leans against the railing, his gaze empty as he looks down at the city with its rivers of traffic and tides of neon lights.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Is it over...? What... should I do now?
He murmurs to no one in particular. He doesn't know if it's a statement or a question. For him, right now, the difference between staying and leaving has become blurred.
Then, he hears a calm voice from behind him.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: If you're unsure what to do... why not start by helping me with a case?
Cassian turns to see you standing by the door, your gaze deep.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Here's the warrant.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Mr. Cassian, time is of the essence. Please come with us.

He doesn't resist when you take him back to the Bureau. Not a single question, not a word of protest. He complies in silence, goes through the security checks, surrenders his belongings, gets assigned to his room, following each step like a machine.
That night, during his registration at the Bureau, Cassian gives a shocking testimony: the Euphoria incident likely involved forces from the Underground, and he encountered their puppets on the ship.

He doubts that the ship's owner, Mr. E, is really dead, but he doesn't think the man could have possessed the power to destroy the entire vessel. The true mastermind behind the massive Mania sorcery must be someone else. But his knowledge ends there. The only person who saw the true culprit was Milly, he adds, but she has yet to regain consciousness.
Cassian isn't in good shape. He can't tell you much, and the questioning is cut short. But you know that there are still many unanswered questions—about Euphoria, and about the man himself.

However, the case is tangled in bureaucracy and politics. Many files are still being requested, and the formal interrogation is repeatedly postponed. For now, all you can do is place him in the detention area for observation.
You'd thought his aimlessness on the rooftop that night was temporary, but your observations over the past few days have deepened your unease.
He is too quiet. It's not the quiet of inaction, but of a life disassembled into a series of trivial, silent, orderly motions, like a performance for an empty room.

His tiny room in the detention area is always spotless. His clothes are folded with almost rigid precision, and his cleaning supplies are meticulously arranged. Even his bath towel is folded into a perfect square and placed in the same corner.

You note that Cassian, despite his wealthy upbringing, is surprisingly good at cleaning and keeping himself tidy. Even in the sparse room, he would always fold his meager set of clothes and wipe every last trace of water from the sink.
He seems to require no human contact, only the comfort of a pristine space and precise movements, as if these alone could fill the emptiness within him.
Every evening, he pours a glass of liquor he never drinks. He just holds it by the rim and sits by the window, staring into space from dusk until late into the night.
The day you go to see him, you find him polishing a brooch. A family crest, carved from dark gemstones and set in silver, burnished until it gleams in his hands.
It's the only thing he treats with genuine care each day.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: It's the only thing I have left of my family. It's beautiful, isn't it?
He speaks softly, his fingers caressing the gem with unusual tenderness. Then he looks up at you, his voice calm like he's stating a simple fact.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: You've been watching me. It's all right. I've known for a while.
You're taken aback, but he merely offers a faint smile before lowering his eyes again.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: There's no need to be so guarded. I won't do anything you don't want me to. I won't cause you any trouble.

His tone is polite, gentle, even considerate. But beneath it, you hear a submission so absolute it feels like the stillness of death. It's not the result of rational self-restraint, but the instinctive response of someone who has completely given up on himself.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: ...We need to talk.
You say it after a moment's silence. He nods, rises to his feet, and silently follows you into the interrogation room.

The interrogation room is sterile, the lights cold. Cassian sits across from you, eyes downcast, quiet as a statue robbed of its soul. You don't cut to the chase. Instead, you flip through a case file and speak in a casual tone, as if to make small talk.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Quite eventful lately, isn't it? After that night on Euphoria, Falke had a complete mental breakdown. They managed to save his life, but his prognosis isn't looking good.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: This is no small matter. His doctor thinks it's trauma from the explosion, but I can't shake the feeling there's more to it than that.
You pause, looking up at him.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: You were on Euphoria that night, Cassian. What do you know?
The enemies still alive... where are they hiding?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I did it.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: ...You're admitting it, just like that?
Your hands pause over the file, your eyes betraying your astonishment. You're taken aback by his frankness, but he simply nods, his tone calm and forthright.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Yes, I used my ability to cause Falke's mental breakdown.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: You can lock me up right now. Prosecute me according to your regulations.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: The case is closed, Chief. You don't need to waste any more time on this. I won't cover up what I've done.

His voice is devoid of emotion, as if he has already passed judgment on himself and is ready to accept any verdict. As if he's actively seeking punishment. But you shake your head, your gaze settling on his gaunt face.
He's just a man who's lost everything, struggling to survive in the wreckage. His methods may have been extreme, nearly costing him his own life, but this isn't the time to be assigning blame.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: I'm not here to press charges. I'm more interested in your help investigating Falke's other crimes than in judging you for what you've done.
For the first time, a flicker of surprise crosses his face.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: The reason Falke survived, despite his mental breakdown, is that one of his powerful old friends took him along during the escape. But that same friend threw him to the wolves the moment they were back in the city.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: He's accusing Falke of being involved in several cold cases. The media is sitting on the story for now, but the news is already spreading like wildfire through Eastside's upper crust.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Falke's finished. His so-called allies are scrambling to distance themselves, pointing fingers, cutting ties, kicking him while he's down. It's quite the show.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Given the stakes, we've joined the investigation. But there are still gaps to fill, crucial information that only insiders can provide. Someone like you.
You pause, studying his tired but composed face.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: None of this surprises you, does it?
Cassian lets out a short, bitter laugh, his eyes full of scorn.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Not at all. That's how they are. They lick the boots of whoever's in power and walk over anyone who falls from grace. One day you're the guest of honor, the next you're a worthless pawn.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: It's exactly what happened to my family. He lifted us to the heavens overnight, then kicked us straight into hell. Now it's his turn. What goes around, comes around.
The contempt in his voice is sharp as a razor's edge. But beneath it, you hear something else: a wound that will never heal, the harsh echo of a cruel era still weighing on his shoulders.
His cynicism isn't baseless. It was forged in blood and fire.

You watch his pale face in the brief silence. His eyes are hard and cold, but you notice the almost imperceptible slump of his shoulders, as though he's running out of the strength to hold himself upright.
You suddenly realize that he seems more lost than ever, a traveler derailed, pushed forward only by inertia. You soften your voice.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: I've heard about what happened back then. In fact, that's why I'm here. Your family was innocent, weren't they?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Of course. Falke used them as scapegoats. My father took his own life. My mother died in the fire. The rest were either framed for crimes they didn't commit or died in "accidents."
Cassian nods, his eyes showing no flicker of emotion, only a frozen darkness.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I was the only one who made it out alive. The only one they managed to save.
The air grows still. You sense that what hangs between you isn't anger or grief, but something deeper, a fathomless, suffocating weight.
He is leaning slightly forward. It seems his body is present, but his soul has drifted away.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: ...So that's why you kept going? To get revenge for them?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Yes.
He nods without a second of hesitation.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I wanted to kill him. But I couldn't control my ability as well as I'd like to. He survived.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: But it's better this way. Letting him live, broken and trapped in his own head... he deserves a fate worse than death.

For the first time, you hear a raw, potent emotion in his voice. A sharp, searing hatred that burns away everything else. You understand, then, that this hatred was the only thing keeping him alive. Revenge was his raison d'être.
The Interrogation room falls into a prolonged silence, until you finally speak in a low voice:

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Now that you've had your revenge... are you happy?
Cassian laughs.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Of course I am. The one thing I kept myself alive for is done. What more could I possibly want?
His tone is so light it's almost cruel, and it makes your chest tighten.

Cassian has accomplished the life goal he set for himself. The vengeful obsession that kept him alive has burned itself out. Now, he's an empty shell that has fulfilled its purpose, with nowhere else to go.
He is no longer living. He merely stays.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: So what did this revenge get you, in the end?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Closure. For my family, who were toyed with and murdered by those in power.
You keep your emotions in check and ask calmly:

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: But what about you?
Cassian falters. A brief, fleeting confusion crosses his face. He falls silent, struggling to find an answer to a question he's never bothered to ask himself.
After a long while, he slowly shakes his head.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I... don't matter. What matters is that I did what I had to do. It's all over.
You look into his eyes, which seem incapable of reflecting a future, and find yourself at a loss for words. You finally realize that what he truly lost wasn't his family or his dignity, but himself.
You speak softly:

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: So you're planning to end it all, is that it?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Perhaps.
He says it with a slight curve of his lips, almost like a smile.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: But they fought so hard to keep you alive. I don't think they did it just for "closure."
In that moment, you see the tips of Cassian's fingers tremble.
But he says nothing, and lowers his head again.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Stop pressing and change the subject

choices.text: Stop pressing and change the subject

steps.content: You're the first to break the silence. You gather the documents on the table and nod at him.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: In any case, thank you for your cooperation. I have the basics now. That's all for today.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: But I'll need you to come with me for the next couple of days.
Cassian looks up, his eyes sharp.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: If you're planning to take me on a field trip and "rekindle my passion for life," please don't trouble yourself.
His voice is cold, laced with undisguised resistance and detachment.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I don't need it. And it would be pointless.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: You misunderstand. I'm going to file a petition to clear your family's name. That old case is clearly tied to Falke, so it falls within the scope of our current investigation. I thought having you there, as a directly affected party, would make our case more compelling.
You pause and look up at him with sincere eyes. You want him to see that you're not doing this out of pity, but out of equality and respect.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: It's long overdue, but at least we can restore their honor. I thought that might be something you'd want to do. Or something you should do. Isn't it?
Cassian clearly never expected to hear anything like this. His eyes widen in surprise.
After a moment, you hear him say:

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Thank you.
